# CV-22 — Home widgets, export and the shortcut sheet

> Branch `t/maciej/cv-22-home-export` · head: see the hand-back · status: built, not landed (migration ready, waiting for its turn)
> Migration: `supabase/migrations/20261016220000_chat_v2_home_export.sql` · applied to the local stack: no (waiting for its turn after CV-13, CV-19, CV-16, CV-18). Dry run: inside a rolled-back transaction as `supabase_admin` with every chat test file (all pass over it except `chat_ops`, `chat_rules` and `statuses`, which fail the same way without it on today's stack: another block's migration is in flight)

## Delivered against the row

- **Catch up widget** (`src/features/dashboard/ui/widgets/catchup-widget.tsx`, shaping in `src/features/chat/catchup/widget.ts`): sizes S and M, what's waiting newest first (avatar, **who** + why, conversation, time), a count, "+N more"; every row and "more" open `/chat?view=catchup`. Reads `useCatchup(store)` (CV-11, your own open items) and the workspace's chat store. Its reads aren't plan-gated (`chat_catchup_open` has no plan check), so it keeps working while chat is paused (AC10.8's widget half; no paused-plan test here).
- **v1's Conversations widget deleted** (`src/features/chat/widget.ts` + test, `chat-widget.tsx`); the catalog entry `chat` is now "Catch up" (gallery icon Inbox, new description).
- **Team widget's now line** (`src/features/chat/home/now-line.tsx`, registered in `widget-registry.tsx` with `registerTeamNowLine`): Active · Away · Focusing (on the task, until …) · the status ("🌴 On vacation until Oct 20"), from `chat_now` (CV-17) and presence on `chat:<ws>`, read as the viewer; nothing for someone with nothing to say. `data-team-now`.
- **Export** (`src/features/chat/export.ts`): every conversation `listChannels` returns, every page of it (`page`, keyset back to the start), chains whose replies the pages didn't carry (`chain`), reactions, the stored bodies verbatim, as `chat.json` + one Markdown file per conversation (`chat/<title>-<id8>.md`); a conversation the server refuses is listed in `incomplete`, never filled in. Files go in as bytes under `chat/files/…` through the `files` hook (paths cleaned: no `..`, no separators). `devices.json`: your own `user_clients` rows (`listMyClients`, `src/lib/notices/clients.ts`). `advanced.ts`: `ExportModuleKey` += `chat`, `devices`; a result may carry `files` (written under `<module>/`); entries are text or bytes; the settings copy names chat.
- **Realtime keys**: `user_statuses` and `chat_members` are keyed by a new `id` (their person columns stay unique: `user_statuses_user_id_key`, `chat_members_channel_user_key`), so a removed row (erasure, an account's cascade, a deleted conversation's cascade) reaches Realtime listeners as an opaque id. The migration asserts no table in `supabase_realtime` is keyed by a person. `realtime.ts` ignores a removed membership (it carries only the id); leaving and removal arrive as `left_at` updates, a deleted conversation on `chat_channels`.
- **Erasure test** extended: `user_clients`, `user_statuses`, `user_saved_statuses` counted in the preview, removed, others untouched, gone with the account; publication-key, uniqueness and grant checks.
- **Shortcut sheet**: Chat's §16 rows by scope (`chatKeyRows` in `src/lib/shortcuts.ts`, section "Chat" in `global-shortcuts-dialog.tsx`).
- Also: Biome's import order in `chat-screen.tsx` (it failed `verify` on the build head).

## Agent's choices (deferred to by Maciej: confirmed for building, may be reconsidered)

- **Opaque keys instead of soft removal** · agent (accepted by the orchestrator) · a removed row reaches Realtime listeners as its key without a read rule; the account's own cascade (and a deleted conversation's) removes `chat_members` / `user_statuses` rows whatever erasure does, so only the key's shape protects people · rejected: soft-removing in erasure (the cascade still removes the rows), leaving these tables out of the publication (live statuses and memberships need it; publication options are per publication, not per table).
- **Your own removal stays live without deletes** · agent · removal is an update of your own row (`chat_op_remove_member` sets `left_at` and `removed_at`; never-joined readers get an inserted row that has already left), which you read under `chat_members_select` (`user_id = auth.uid()`), so `realtime.ts` reports `member-left` from that update; a deleted conversation arrives on `chat_channels`; the access check (`chat_sync_ids`) stays the truth on every rejoin · rejected: mapping your own membership row ids in the store (a second source of truth for the same fact).
- **Nothing else depends on the old keys** · checked: no `onConflict` on either table in the app, no `ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT` or key-name reference in migrations (including CV-13/16/18/19's branches), moduo-mcp reads neither table, the app's `chat_members` reads order by `(channel_id, user_id)`, which stays unique. Prod: the default fills every row with its own id in the same transaction, the migration checks no id repeats before swapping, and the old key's name `chat_members_pkey` (prod dump) is dropped and reused in one `ALTER TABLE`; a second run changes nothing.
- **The widget keeps type id `chat`** · agent · saved dashboards keep their widget with no data migration · rejected: a new `catchup` type plus a migration of saved layouts. A saved L instance draws as M (sizes are S and M).
- **The count sits on a "Waiting for you" label line** · agent · the shared widget frame has no count slot in its header (frame 8 puts it there) · rejected: changing the shared `WidgetFrame`.
- **Widget words**: frame 8's "sent you a message" and "replied in your chain" for a person's lines, Catch up's own words for the rest; the conversation follows a channel's line ("mentioned you · Acme rebrand"), never a direct message's · rejected: the Catch up list's "direct message".
- **The now line holds presence through the same shared store** the top bar's Chat tab already holds app-wide (`chat-tab.ts`), so Home joins no new topic and tracks nothing new.
- **The shortcut sheet scrolls** (`max-h-[85vh]`, the repo's dialog precedent) so it fits the 1024×700 minimum window.
- **The export pages until an empty page**, not until a short one: the server may answer fewer than asked.
- **Every row opens Catch up** (not the item) · the brief's "opening Catch up"; Catch up has no deep link to an item yet.
- **"Active" when reachable** in the now line (frame 8), nothing when offline with nothing to say.
- **Export of `user_clients`: yes** (`devices.json`, your own rows only) · the orchestrator's rule reverses CV-6a's choice.
- **Export Markdown keeps the stored text** as written (references stay as their links) · lossless; the JSON is the exact row · rejected: rendering references to names (loses what they point at).
- **Files and custom emoji**: the `files` hook is ready; CV-9 (attachments) and CV-20 (custom emoji) aren't on the build branch, so no file is written yet, and erasure's "custom emoji `created_by` → null" waits for CV-20's table.

## Gotchas (area: supabase | ui)

- supabase: Realtime sends a removed row's key to listeners without a read rule (`realtime.apply_rls` skips the check for deletes and keeps the key columns); a filtered subscription whose filter column isn't in the key gets no deletes at all. Key published tables by their own row id.
- ui: `ExportBundle.entries` are text or bytes now; tests that `JSON.parse` an entry need `String(…)`.

## For later blocks

- **CV-9 / CV-20:** fill `ChatExportReads.files` (`src/features/chat/export.ts`) with your attachments and emoji images (`{ path, bytes }`, paths like `attachments/<message>/<name>`, `emoji/<name>.<ext>`), from `advanced-section.tsx`'s chat read; CV-20: erasure sets a custom emoji's `created_by` to null and `chat_erasure.test.sql` checks it.
- **Any block publishing a table:** key it by its own id (the migration's assert and `chat_erasure.test.sql` fail otherwise).
- **CV-21:** the widgets read through the app's session reads; MCP stays on its own reads.
